        Paper steps → coordinate route → expressed algorithm → executable block program → shape function → data filtering.

        Evidence of understanding

        Predict before running, trace the first divergence and explain why the fix works with new inputs.

        Misconceptions and support

        Counter reset inside a loop or > confused with ≥: trace each row and variable value.

        Transfer beyond the game

        Create a small executable block program; paper work prepares, but does not replace programming objectives.

        Visible reward

        The star machine gains a module; original programs become visible creations.

        Design proposal; requires teacher review and child pilots. No automatic mastery certification.

        Monsters and roles

        These are briefs for later illustration, not generated character artwork. No monster punishes mistakes or withdraws friendship when a child needs help.

        Momo

        Addition, subtraction and equal groups

        An enthusiastic teammate who thinks aloud and tries different approaches.

        «We can build it and see what happens.»

        Retain the chosen sketch's mint rounded body, two large eyes, little horns and friendly tooth; blocks are tools.

        Do not praise speed or demand excitement after every task.

        Tilly

        Counting, quantity and place value

        Patient and curious; helps point, organise and notice that quantity is unchanged.

        «One thing, one counting word. We have time.»

        Retain the small apricot monster and expression from the sketch; add a seed bag and tens bundles.

        Do not infantilise older learners using small-number support; offer a calmer presentation.

        Ozzy

        Comparison, patterns and relationships

        An observant explorer who asks what is the same and what differs without judging.

        «What in the model shows that both sides are equal?»

        Retain the lilac body, single large eye and sketch silhouette; add a simple notebook, never a scary guard.

        Do not link body features to intelligence; the child may choose another buddy.

        Mira

        Fractions, decimals and percentages

        A caring island builder who always asks what counts as the whole.

        «Let's agree on the whole first.»

        New character brief: a soft wave silhouette, two eyes and a bag of equal-length fraction strips; readable at small sizes.

        Do not make food the only fraction model or call unequal pieces fair.

        Tova

        Shape, space and symmetry

        A creative builder who rotates, folds and tests rather than guessing by appearance.

        «Turn the shape. Are its properties the same?»

        New brief: a slightly angular but soft body, two different little horns and a paper shape; no dangerous tools.

        Never use colour alone to distinguish shapes or parts.

        Otto

        Measurement, units and time

        A calm ferry planner who estimates before measuring and likes clear units.

        «What are we measuring—and which unit fits?»

        New brief: a broad soft silhouette with a clock and tape measure; friendly, not a military captain.

        The clock is learning content, not a timer that pressures the child.

        Nori

        Data, chance and financial reasoning

        A friendly investigator who asks where numbers came from and what a deal hides.

        «What do these numbers tell us—and what don't they?»

        New brief: a yellow monster with a large pocket and data cards; no wealth-status or gambling imagery.

        Do not collect other children's data to make the game realistic.

        Zipp

        Algorithms, programming and debugging

        A slightly scatterbrained inventor who shows their own mistakes and fixes the first divergence systematically.

        «I missed a step. Can we trace it together?»

        New brief: a soft star-like body with a paper program in a pocket; no required flashing eyes or lights.

        Never present bugs as stupidity; they tell us about the program.

        Progression and rewards

        Learning status—not XP as evidence

        Unassessed → exploring → supported → independent → transferred → checked later. Status belongs to a learning step and representation, not to the child. A correct answer after a hint is 'supported'. A later check may reveal a need without removing collected pages or stamps.

        Mastery gate and adult role

        Pilot proposal: at least three varied items over two sessions, two representations, an explanation and a new context; revisit after a few days. This is not a validated threshold. Oral/practical explanations require a simple adult rubric: relation, model, strategy and check. Teachers may override with a visible reason.

        Next-quest rule

        Prioritise confirmed support needed for a relevant step, then a short due review, then the next suitable step in the chosen region. Use one brief repair block before a return test. Repeated uncertainty becomes visible to the teacher, not an endless automatic loop. One error alone never triggers a whole-level downgrade.

        Two tracks: adventure and understanding

        Adventure stamps recognise a meaningful completed quest, including supported work. Skill badges require learning evidence. Time, clicks, streaks and currency never determine mastery. 'You explored' and 'you can explain' are different, equally valued achievements.

        Badges and collection

        Retain Number finder, Curious thinker and Putting together from the sketch. Add Group builder, Fair sharer, Whole-and-part explorer, Balance explainer, Measurement investigator and Bug finder. Each badge page shows its skill, example and observed evidence—not rank or age. Buddy pages open at first meeting, never behind purchases.

        A reward economy without purchases

        No currency is needed initially. Give one unique story piece per new quest; replay adds a practice entry, not infinite points. Children choose garden decorations, notebook patterns or buddy accessories. All are cosmetic and deterministic: no loot boxes, adverts, paid hints or daily streak penalties.

        Celebration, breaks and mistakes

        Optional brief celebration after a solution or well-explained correction. Sound and extra motion default off; text is always available. Say 'that works' or 'let's build it', not 'almost' when the answer is far off. No lives, timers, leaderboards or lost friendship. Break message: 'We'll continue when you want'.

        Example: multiplication with a gap

        The child answers 7 for 3×4. Momo asks what 3 and 4 mean and offers three groups of four blocks. After a supported 12, record 'supported' and award one story token. Next use 2×5 in another form, then revisit a new 3×4 context. Only later can varied independent answers and explanations support a Group builder badge.

        Implementation baseline

        Eggs, growth and monster collection

        Starting a chapter gives an egg. Completing at least half its tasks hatches it; each newly completed task automatically feeds it and fills the growth bar. Completing the chapter gives a fully grown monster. Unique task IDs count once only. Mistakes, help, revisits and breaks never remove growth. Progress and started chapters are held in memory while the page is open and can be saved as a versioned QR code or text code that can be loaded again. Progress is not stored in the browser; only settings for sound, voice and motion are remembered. Collection is not mastery assessment.

        Monster tutoring and chapter ideas

        Help opens a four-step tutorial for each of the 24 topics: explanation, worked example, independent practice and support for the current game task. Practice awards no game tokens and does not change the game answer. Children can go back or close at any point; help use is recorded as supported. Each of eight chapters has a mathematical fun fact and a separately labelled imagination or exploration prompt.

        One fraction, three representations

        The 18 fraction tasks and half-cargo introduction vary between cakes, groups and number lines. Switching views preserves answers and selections. Comparisons keep the whole and scale fixed. Groups use equal parts; the number line shows distance from zero, including fractions above one. Part selections stay synchronized with the answer controls.

        The solution on the reflection graph

        After a correct answer, reflected points and relevant edges appear on the existing grid. Dashed guides connect original and image; single-point tasks label equal distances from the axis. Points on the axis remain in place. Incorrect answers do not reveal the plot; explicitly requesting the worked solution also reveals it.

        Sharing with movable pieces

        Seven sharing tasks have a free play board with large pieces and recipients. Children can drag between the tray and buckets, rearrange freely, or select a piece then a destination by touch or keyboard. Counts show the actual distribution, not the solution. Leftovers may remain on the tray. Language changes and answer attempts preserve the arrangement; new tasks and restart reset it. The board does not fill the number field or award tokens automatically.

        From choosing to entering the answer

        Multiplication starts with multiple choice; from the second task, children enter the number themselves. Later numeric tasks in counting, place value, patterns, fractions, measurement and geometry also require answers without options. Sorting and selecting shapes or strategies remain when the action itself is the learning goal. Decimal commas and dots and equivalent fractions such as 3/8 are accepted. Enter or Check submits the answer. Mistakes provide support and a retry without penalties.

        Dedicated game screen and accessibility

        The learner flow is map → game → map, with icons and short names. Long curriculum explanations live in the adult view. Language and theme sit in settings. Play shows one task at a time; allow scrolling when small screens or magnification require it, never clip content. The target is WCAG 2.2 AA. Automated checks alone do not establish conformance: release requires manual assessment of all applicable criteria, screen readers, keyboard, contrast, magnification and physical devices.

        Scope of the playable introductions

        Each of 24 games has nine tasks across exploration, strategy and use in new contexts: 216 tasks with task-specific support, not complete coverage of every learning step or curriculum action. Levels are freely selectable and do not certify mastery. Correct responses earn trial tokens; merely displaying a solution does not. Further work must add practical explanations, confirmed diagnostics and delayed review.

        Phones and tablets from the start

        Mobile first: support narrow phones, tablets and both orientations without horizontal scrolling. Large touch targets, answers without swiping or hover, and a numeric keyboard where appropriate. Never lock orientation or disable zoom. Use a vertical phone trail; keep tasks, hints and answers readable on split-screen tablets. The virtual keyboard must not hide submission. Browser emulation is an initial check only: later test real iPad/Safari and Android/Chrome, including screen readers and virtual keyboards.

        A reusable game framework

        Separate content from mechanics. A shared frame has a buddy, short goal, model area, answer, graduated hint, feedback, calm next step and ending. Adapters cover selection, groups, number lines, balance, grids, tables and programs. Each variant references a step ID and approved item template; do not duplicate 69 apps.

        Data and events

        QuestInstance: ID, template version, seed, locale, objective/step, parameters, mathematical answer and accepted forms. Attempt: quest ID, response, prior support, result and chosen model. Evidence: independent/supported, rubric, observer and date. Award: unique learner+quest+awardType key. Production requires server-side answer validation and idempotency; the client is not authoritative.

        Translation without changing mathematics

        Use stable string keys for nn, nb and en. Numbers and formulas are data, not embedded translated text. Use Intl for numbers, dates and plurals; Norwegian decimal commas and English points. Accept valid local input without ambiguous parsing. Language changes preserve quest ID, parameters, support history and progress. Missing strings fail the build, rather than silently falling back to English.

        Accessibility and sensory choices

        Use 44 px targets, visible focus and keyboard alternatives to dragging. No information only in colour, sound or motion. Grids have text/buttons; charts have tables. Optional narration retains text and uses the right language voice, with an explicit unavailable state. Reduce buddy presence and respect motion preferences. Test 200% zoom and narrow phones.

        Character kit for later visual production

        Shared style: soft, slightly silly monsters; lavender, mint, apricot, lilac and yellow; simple silhouettes and calm white reading surfaces. Each needs neutral, thinking, encouraging and calm-celebration poses, a small avatar, full-body art and light/dark contrast checks. No sadness or anger triggered by learner errors. Retain Momo/Tilly/Ozzy; new characters are briefs for approval.

        Teacher/parent surface

        Show objective/step, support use, specific error pattern, uncertainty and a recommended physical quest. No public ranking or global ability labels. Distinguish missing evidence from difficulty. Confirm oral/practical rubrics manually; AI interpretation must not diagnose or independently certify full mastery.

        Child data and production boundary

        This page runs without login and without storing progress on the device; only settings for sound, voice and motion are remembered by the browser. To continue later you create a QR code or text code that contains only completed task IDs, started chapters, arcade results and the language choice—no names, answer histories or identity. Anyone holding the code can read the progress, so keep it as you would any private picture. Before a real portal, establish lawful basis, parent/school roles, data minimisation, deletion/export and secure authentication.

        Learning-content quality gate

        All 69 objectives link to concepts, but a concept is not full coverage in practice. Before publishing, trace every verb and representation to steps and actual items; validate answers, parameters, distractors and scaffolds in each language. Pilot with children and teachers, especially transfer after support. Tune thresholds and rewards using learning evidence, not engagement alone.

        Proposed delivery sequence

        1. Welcome and foundations

        Tilly counting, Ozzy comparison, Momo addition/subtraction and equality. nn/nb/en, large buttons, a physical quest and one unique reward. Import objective wording and steps from the curriculum map.

        2. One complete multiplication pathway

        Build groups → array → factor meaning → table selection/fluency → distributivity → real-world problem → later check. Repair addition confusion with a concrete model. Connect initial division quests. This is the first complete vertical learning slice.

        3. Fractions and measurement with recovery

        Four fraction meanings, equivalence and whole-number misconceptions; area/perimeter and unit errors. Test support → parallel item → return. Build teacher observation before any mastery automation.

        4. Expand the academy

        Geometry, data, finance and executable programming. Review all 24 concepts against all 69 objectives and 225 foundation/map steps. New monster artwork follows approved briefs; this baseline does not generate it.

        Free software; its official site confirms open development in KDE. No code or tasks copied.

        Bounded activities, level selection and matching expressions to representations. We do not adopt timed or competitive variants.

        The Math Learning Center · Number Pieces

        Free visual tool; not verified as open source here. General teaching inspiration only.

        Tens and ones, regrouping and rectangular multiplication models.

        The Math Learning Center · Geoboard

        Free visual tool; not verified as open source here. No drawings or wording copied.

        A common grid for area, perimeter, rotation and reflection; compare changing and invariant properties.

        PhET · Fractions Intro source archive
